subject.title: fix(agents): bound finished bash process session retention

question: Should OpenClaw accept early eviction of completed process poll/log records before the job TTL when the proposed 50-session or 2,000,000-character budget is exceeded?
rationale: The patch correctly bounds gateway memory, but the limits intentionally narrow the existing delayed-poll availability window; code review cannot choose that compatibility contract for maintainers.

options.title: Accept bounded eviction
options.body: Land the internal budgets and accept oldest-first early expiry during unusually bursty shell workloads.

options.title: Revise the budgets
options.body: Choose larger internal limits or a different retention design after defining the minimum delayed-poll availability window.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded eviction
recommendation.body: Land the internal budgets and accept oldest-first early expiry during unusually bursty shell workloads.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history connects Peter to merged session-lifecycle behavior adjacent to this cleanup boundary, making him the strongest available routing candidate for the compatibility choice.
